covers: The block-header bytes the uPD7759 decodes, from the host in slave mode

entries.name: end of sample
entries.description: Header 0x00: ends the sample, or is a short silence before any data.
entries.behaviour: In the block-header state, if a non-zero header was already seen since the address bytes, the chip goes idle. Otherwise it is a 1024-clock silence and another header follows. Either way the sample value and ADPCM step state reset to zero; no bytes follow.

entries.name: silence
entries.description: Header 00dddddd: a silence, then the next header.
entries.behaviour: Lasts (value + 1) x 1024 chip clocks and resets the sample value and ADPCM step state to zero. No bytes follow.

entries.name: play 256 nibbles
entries.description: Header 01ffffff: plays the next 128 bytes as 256 ADPCM nibbles.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 5 plus one are the rate; each nibble lasts rate x 4 chip clocks, high nibble of each byte first. Then the next byte is a header.

entries.name: play n nibbles
entries.description: Header 10ffffff: a count byte follows, then that many ADPCM nibbles.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 5 plus one are the rate, as for 0x40. The next byte N gives N+1 nibbles, so N/2+1 data bytes follow, high nibble first; an odd count ignores the last byte's low nibble. Then the next byte is a header.

entries.name: repeat marker
entries.description: Header 11---rrr: sets a repeat count; the next byte is a normal header.
entries.behaviour: Count is (value & 7) + 1 and bits 3 to 5 are unused; 0xFF is this marker with count 8. Each later header while the count is non-zero decrements it and rewinds the ROM offset, which only matters in stand-alone mode, so a slave host resends the repeated bytes itself.
